title: Bank Deposit Delay Uplift on Shortfall Deliveries after a Long Wait
content:
When the recipient of a Bank Deposit transfer has waited a long time since the payout that came up short, the make-good delivery rate of the shortfall delivery is raised by a delay uplift.

## How the wait is measured

The wait is counted in calendar days from the date of the payout that came up short (the date of the latest payout sent, as the transfer's ledger shows it) to the handling date.

## Clause

When the wait reaches 21 days and the tier pays out on a batch rail (one or more delivery business days), the uplift accrues 0.25 percent for every whole week of the wait, never more than an uplift cap of 2.00 percent; when the wait reaches 21 days and the tier pays out in real time (no delivery business days), the uplift is a flat 0.50 percent; a shorter wait carries no delay uplift.

## Which tiers count as batch and as real time

| Tier | Delivery business days | Treated as |
|---|---|---|
| Bank Deposit Economy | 3 | batch rail |
| Bank Deposit Standard | 1 | batch rail |
| Bank Deposit Express | 0 | real time |
| Bank Deposit Express Plus | 0 | real time |
| Bank Deposit Large Amount | 1 | batch rail |
| Bank Deposit International Wire | 2 | batch rail |

## Uplift by wait (hypothetical waits)

| Wait in calendar days | Batch-rail tier | Real-time tier |
|---|---|---|
| 20 | none | none |
| 21 (3 whole weeks) | 0.75 percent | 0.50 percent |
| 27 (3 whole weeks) | 0.75 percent | 0.50 percent |
| 28 (4 whole weeks) | 1.00 percent | 0.50 percent |
| 56 (8 whole weeks) | 2.00 percent | 0.50 percent |
| 63 (9 whole weeks) | 2.00 percent (2.25 held at the cap) | 0.50 percent |

A whole week is each complete run of seven days in the wait.
